div.style: color: rgb(16, 42, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(6, 64, 43) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p: A seam between parts

div.style: color: rgb(90, 58, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(92, 34, 6) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(16, 42, 67) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
Protein sequence → ESM-C 600M
One amino-acid string per target; median 454
residues, longest 34,350. Out comes one vector
per residue, from 573,632,640 frozen weights.
They stay frozen because 572 effective target units
cannot fine-tune a model this size without fitting
the targets rather than the binding.

v2 keeps four layers, not one, spaced through the
36-block stack. The final layer is the one most
specialised for ESM-C's own masked-token objective,
rather than the one richest in structure.

div.style: color: rgb(16, 42, 67) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
Residue cache · 14.0 → 56 GiB
All 10,820 targets encoded once, reproducing
bit-for-bit, which is what makes reuse safe.

The cache declares its own layer set and every
reader asks it. Measured: the last of the four
blocks is bit-identical to the one-layer cache,
so a four-layer run starts from what v1 saw.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
Ligand SMILES → line graph + knowledge
One standardized string per molecule, rewritten so
each bond is a node. Two extra nodes hold a
512-bit fingerprint and 200 computed properties.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
LiGhT · 8 layers, 8 heads, width 96
Each bond looks at bonds up to five
atoms away. Bond-to-bond attention
is kept for iBAM.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Summary → 288
Fingerprint node, property node, mean
over bonds. Never blended.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
Pre-training · done
Hide one knowledge node, rebuild it from the molecule
plus the other. 540,166 molecules, all of them from the
training set, so held-out data and the sealed panels are
excluded. Held-out loss 0.2002, 48.8% under a
molecule-blind guess.

div.style: color: rgb(6, 64, 43) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
The seam: what the ligand hands over
One vector per bond, plus two masks: real rather than padding, and drawable on a
molecule or not. Knowledge nodes are real but not drawable, and conflating those two
questions is what forced them to be discarded before.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Protein → 256
v2: LayerMix picks a weighted blend of the four
cached layers first, one weight each. Starts at
99.9% last layer, so it begins as v1. Then 1152
narrows to 256, a 4.5x squeeze rather than 12x.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Bonds → 256
96 per bond, normalized.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Summary → 3 × 256
Each part projected on its own, so the
fingerprint is never averaged in with
the properties.

div.style: color: rgb(90, 58, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
v2: assay conditions → 256 · 50 in
pH/temperature bucket, IC50 tier, source
class, confidence. IC50 is 72.2% of the
corpus and is not a constant of the pair:
it moves with substrate and enzyme
concentration, and v1 never read it.
Group ids excluded, they lead to the label.

div.style: color: rgb(90, 58, 0) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
Knowledge and assay conditioning · FiLM · 788,992
Global properties rescale every residue and bond rather than being appended at the end:
an appended vector can be ignored, a multiplied one cannot. Starts as an exact no-op, so
switching it off compares the same model, not a new draw.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Protein looks at ligand
Each residue spreads attention over the
molecule's bonds. 256 → 512 → 256.

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Two separate sets of weights, side by
side. Neither sees the other's output,
and one is not the transpose of the other.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Ligand looks at protein
Each bond spreads attention over the
residues. 256 → 512 → 256.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
v2: pooled by relevance, not averaged · 526,344 · 1,536 numbers, six blocks
Fused residues · fused bonds · protein before fusion · fingerprint · properties · bond average.
A binding site is ~20-30 residues of a median 454, so v1 averaged the signal away
by a factor of 15 to 20. Four heads now score each residue instead. Exactly equal to
the mean at initialisation, so the change is an ablation and not a different model.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(92, 34, 6) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
Score only the endpoint that was measured
Kd, Ki and IC50 are different experiments and are never mixed. A measurement that does not
exist gets no stand-in value, because no such value is representable.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Exact
Error under the lab's own repeat
scatter is free: 0.945 Kd, 0.641 Ki,
0.671 IC50.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Censored · 18.5% of training pairs
'Weaker than 10 µM'. Penalized for
crossing the bound, never for landing
inside it.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Lower-confidence
Weighted 0.25 and kept structurally
apart, so they cannot reach the
main term.

div.style: color: rgb(74, 59, 0) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Which of two is better · weight 0.1
Off in v1, on in v2. Inside one assay only,
and only when the gap beats that endpoint's
repeat scatter.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
v1 trained and measured · v2 untrained · one seed
Budget 30 epochs, selected at epoch 2; val RMSE rose every epoch after, so three
epochs were useful and the rest is overfitting.

All 186,923 exact val labels, 95% intervals from a cluster bootstrap over 3,202 protein
components: RMSE 1.2432 (1.220 to 1.268) · concordance 0.730 · Spearman 0.637 ·
AUROC 0.806 · AUPRC 0.749 on a 0.424 baseline.

An endpoint-mean guess scores 1.4437 and the noise floor is 0.670, so v1 captures
25.9% of the learnable span. Closing that gap is what v2 is for.

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
iBAM: what the model looked at · unblocked
Every map kept per layer and per head, unaveraged:
32 protein-ligand (2 layers × 8 heads × 2 directions)
and 64 bond-bond (8 LiGhT layers × 8 heads).

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Ensemble · blocked, 1 of 3
Needs three separately trained models.
Three passes over one model are refused
in code, so a single seed buys nothing here.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Calibrated intervals · blocked
Split conformal on a held-apart slice.
Needs the ensemble above, so it waits on
seeds 2 and 3. Too few points returns a
status, never an invented interval.

div.style: color: rgb(11, 60, 82) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Is this input familiar?
Similarity to training molecules only,
because an ensemble can agree
confidently about the unseen.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 34, 6) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Benchmark lock
Refuses to score on the sealed panels when
training overlaps them. Measured, not guessed
from the split's name: random 60 to 100%,
cold-target 66 to 69%, time-based 0%. Only
the last qualifies. Opening cannot be undone.

div.style: color: rgb(51, 51, 51) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
Drug fishing, an evaluation, not a part
3,721 targets · 81,971 actives · 37,187 measured
inactives · 1,926,939 matched decoys. A question
asked of a finished model, so it needs no tower.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
What it would be told
Target, endpoint, seed molecule,
what the model attended to, and
the scaffold to preserve.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
Discrete graph diffusion
Atoms and bonds corrupted by category, never by
Gaussian noise on a one-hot: carbon is not between
nitrogen and oxygen. Noise decays to the training
marginal, so the fully-noised graph is already
element-plausible.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Back to a real molecule
RDKit decode, sanitize, scaffold re-checked by
atom mapping rather than substructure match:
a scaffold rebuilt elsewhere passes a match and
is still a failure. Validity reported before and
after sanitizing, so the sanitizer's rescues are
not credited to the model.

div.style: color: rgb(92, 34, 6) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center;

span.p:
Never shown the answer it predicts.
Sampling is not differentiable, so
gradients stop here.

div.style: color: rgb(79, 36, 67) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 300px; text-align: center; width: 300px;

span.p:
The full objective · all terms now built
Affinity + ranking + retrieval + generation +
measured-change. Retrieval never treats an unmeasured
pair as a nonbinder. The delta head is antisymmetric
and exactly zero for A vs A, by construction.

svg.text: BINDRA-v2 · 7,393,163 trainable parameters · v1 measured, v2 built and untrained
